ap_microeconomics-m01.stem: For a firm in the short run, which type of cost is the following? The monthly rent on a factory building under a one-year lease.

options.text: This is a sunk cost that should be ignored when deciding on output.
options.why: Treats a cost as sunk although it affects the cost curves; a sunk cost cannot be recovered but fixed costs still count in the short run.

options.text: This is a fixed cost, because it does not change with the quantity of output in the short run.
options.why: Fixed costs do not vary with output in the short run; variable costs do.

options.text: This is an implicit cost, because no cash payment is made.
options.why: Confuses fixed and variable with explicit and implicit costs; this cost is a cash payment.

options.text: This is a marginal cost, because it is paid each period.
options.why: Confuses the timing of payment with the change in cost from one more unit.

options.text: This is an opportunity cost only if the firm is profitable.
options.why: Ties opportunity cost to profitability, which is unrelated.

facts: cost=The monthly rent on a factory

ap_microeconomics-m02.stem: Why does a competitive market tend to provide too little of a pure public good?

options.text: The marginal cost of serving one more user is high, so firms avoid providing it.
options.why: Public goods have near-zero marginal cost of serving another user.

options.text: People can use it without paying, so firms cannot earn enough revenue to supply it.
options.why: Non-excludability creates a free-rider problem: people have no incentive to pay, so the market underprovides the public good.

options.text: Public goods have no social benefit, so no one wants them.
options.why: Public goods usually have large social benefits.

options.text: Governments always provide public goods at zero cost to taxpayers.
options.why: Governments finance public goods through taxes; they are not costless.

options.text: Consumers value public goods less than they value private goods.
options.why: Valuation is not the reason; the inability to exclude non-payers is the reason.

ap_microeconomics-m03.stem: Which type of economic system is best described as follows? A central planning agency decides what goods are produced, how many are produced, and who receives them, and firms follow its quotas.

options.text: Traditional economy
options.why: Treats habit and custom as the allocation method, which the description does not mention.

options.text: Command economy
options.why: The described allocation method is characteristic of a command economy.

options.text: Mixed economy
options.why: Treats the economy as a mix of market exchange and government direction, but the description does not describe both.

options.text: Laissez-faire monopoly
options.why: Confuses an economic system with a market structure; a monopoly is a market structure, not a way to answer the three basic economic questions.

options.text: Market economy
options.why: Assumes prices and voluntary exchange alone drive all decisions, although the description names central direction, a mixed role for government, or custom.

options.why: Treats habit and custom as the allocation method, which the description does not mention.

options.text: Laissez-faire monopoly
options.why: Confuses an economic system with a market structure; a monopoly is a market structure, not a way to answer the three basic economic questions.

options.text: Market economy
options.why: Assumes prices and voluntary exchange alone drive all decisions, although the description names central direction, a mixed role for government, or custom.

options.text: Command economy
options.why: Takes government direction of every decision as the defining feature, which the description does not contain.

options.text: Mixed economy
options.why: The described allocation method is characteristic of a mixed economy.
